story_and_acs:
Monitor transactions for suspicious activity. As a compliance analyst, I want completed transactions checked against the monitoring rules, so that suspicious activity is spotted and investigated.
AC1: Every completed deposit, withdrawal and transfer is checked against the monitoring rules within 5 minutes of completing.
AC2: A single transaction of more than 5,000.00 raises alert LARGE_TXN. For a customer with a HIGH risk rating the amount is more than 2,500.00.
AC3: Three or more deposits within any 24 hours, each from 4,500.00 to 4,999.99, raise alert STRUCTURING.
AC4: More than 10 transfers out in one calendar day, in the customer's time zone, raise alert VELOCITY.
AC5: A transfer to or from a country on the high-risk country list raises alert HIGH_RISK_COUNTRY, whatever the amount.
AC6: A deposit followed within 48 hours by transfers out totalling 90% or more of that deposit raises alert RAPID_MOVEMENT.
AC7: One transaction can raise more than one alert. Each alert is recorded separately with the customer, the transaction, the rule and the date and time.
AC8: Two or more alerts for the same customer within 30 days open a case for an analyst. A single alert does not open a case.
AC9: Alerts and cases are never shown or mentioned to the customer.

Covers: AC1

Steps: Complete a transfer. / Observe the time it completes and the time it is checked against the monitoring rules.
Expected: The completed transfer is checked against the monitoring rules no later than five minutes after completion.

story_and_acs:
Analyst decision on a referred application. As a compliance analyst, I want to approve or reject applications referred for review, so that only applications that pass our checks are opened.
AC1: Only a compliance analyst can approve or reject an application with status PENDING_REVIEW.
AC2: An analyst cannot decide an application they submitted on behalf of a customer.
AC3: Rejecting an application requires a reason chosen from the reason list.
AC4: Each decision is recorded with the analyst's ID, the date and time, the decision and the reason.
AC5: The applicant is emailed the outcome within 1 business day of the decision.
AC6: The decision time is shown to staff in 24-hour format in the analyst's time zone (for example 14:05), and to the applicant in 12-hour format with AM or PM in the applicant's time zone (for example 2:05 PM). A decision at midnight is shown as 00:00 to staff and 12:00 AM to the applicant.

story_and_acs:
Enhanced due diligence on a large first deposit. As a compliance analyst, I want large first deposits checked, so that the source of the money is understood.
AC1: A first deposit of more than 10,000.00 made within 30 days of the account opening date opens an EDD case.
AC2: A first deposit of exactly 10,000.00 does not open an EDD case.
AC3: When an EDD case is opened, the customer is asked for a source-of-funds document, which must be received within 14 days.
AC4: If the source-of-funds document is not received within 14 days, the account status changes to FROZEN.
AC5: A frozen account cannot make withdrawals or transfers until an analyst closes the EDD case.

story_and_acs:
Onboard a business customer. As a compliance officer, I want to identify the directors and beneficial owners of a business applicant, so that we know who owns and controls every business customer.
AC1: A business application needs the company name, the company registration number and the country of registration. An application missing any of these cannot be submitted.
AC2: Every director must be named, with their full name and date of birth. At least one director is required.
AC3: Every beneficial owner must be identified. A beneficial owner is a person who owns or controls more than 25% of the company, directly or indirectly. A person with exactly 25% is not a beneficial owner.
AC4: Indirect ownership is worked out through each company in the chain by multiplying the percentages: a person who owns 50% of a company that owns 60% of the applicant owns 30% of the applicant. A person's direct and indirect percentages are added together.
AC5: Every director and beneficial owner is screened against the sanctions list and the PEP list in the same way as an individual applicant. A match on any one of them applies to the whole application.
AC6: If no person owns or controls more than 25%, the most senior director is recorded as the beneficial owner and the application is flagged NO_OWNER_ABOVE_THRESHOLD.

Steps: Record a person as owning 24.99% of the applicant. / Review the beneficial-owner identification and application flag.
Expected: The 24.99% owner is not identified as a beneficial owner. The most senior director is recorded as the beneficial owner, and the application is flagged NO_OWNER_ABOVE_THRESHOLD.

story_and_acs:
Calculate the customer risk rating. As a compliance officer, I want every new customer given a risk rating, so that the level of checks matches the risk.
AC1: The risk score is a whole number from 0 to 100.
AC2: A score from 0 to 39 is LOW, from 40 to 69 is MEDIUM, and from 70 to 100 is HIGH.
AC3: A customer whose country of residence is on the high-risk country list has 30 points added, and the score is capped at 100. The list is maintained by the compliance team; the rating uses the list in force on the day the rating is calculated.
AC4: A HIGH rating opens an EDD (enhanced due diligence) case before the account is opened. The applicant is asked for a source-of-funds document, and the account is opened only after an analyst approves the EDD case.
